title: bug: PowerShell Invoke-MoeRpc unwraps singleton JSON arrays into objects
description: On Windows PowerShell 5.1, Invoke-MoeRpc's `return ($text | ConvertFrom-Json)` unrolls `[ {profile:'verified-local',ready:true,missingCapabilities:[]} ]` into PSCustomObject (reproduced with its exact return expression). CQ-M07n1's approved downstream object/type predicate cannot distinguish this malformed wire array from a valid readiness object; audit scalar/object RPC consumers and preserve wire shape without changing existing list callers.

implementationPlan.description:
Audit every Invoke-MoeRpc caller; the governor asked to 'audit each Invoke-MoeRpc caller to show it'. No code change is expected. The result goes in the step note and the complete_task summary.

List the callers at your base: `grep -nE "Invoke-MoeRpc(Unserved)?\b|Invoke-MoeLandLeaseRpc|Send-MoeEvidence" scripts/moe-agent.ps1`. For each call site record the line, the tool, how the reply is consumed, and the verdict. The facts the audit rests on were checked at 9578c609 plus n1's bytes:
- 27 tools reach Invoke-MoeRpc: add_comment, chat_channels, chat_join, chat_read, chat_send, chat_wait, claim_next_task, deregister_worker, enter_governance, finalize_attempt, get_commit_scope, get_context, get_pending_questions, lease_account, list_tasks, reattach_attempt, record_candidate, record_check_run, record_commit, record_delivery_receipt, release_task, report_account_usage, report_blocked, acquire_resource, wait_for_resource, release_resource, and n1's get_execution_readiness.
- Each handler (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/<Name>.ts) returns a JSON object; none has a top-level `return [`. McpAdapter serializes it with JSON.stringify (server/McpAdapter.ts:313). So no real reply is a top-level array, no caller's behaviour changes on real traffic, and there is no existing list caller to preserve.
- No caller pipes or enumerates the return: `Invoke-MoeRpc ... | ForEach-Object/Where-Object`, `@(Invoke-MoeRpc ...)` and `foreach (... in (Invoke-MoeRpc ...))` have 0 hits. The `| Out-Null` callers discard it.
- Malformed replies only (the daemon never sends them): a one-element array now reaches object consumers as an array.
  - Member access still reads through it (`$r.success`). The exception is a field named like an array member: `$r.count` would read the array's length.
  - Get-MoeProp and PSObject.Properties reads (Send-MoeEvidence, Test-MoeClaimNoTeam, Get-MoeWorkspaceClaim, n1's gate) see no field and take their failure branch.
  - An empty array is falsy like the old $null, but `$null -eq @()` is not true. Name each `$null -eq $r` caller and show that its next check still rejects the empty array. For example, in Send-MoeEvidence, Get-MoeProp 'success' is not a bool, so it throws 'invalid payload acknowledgement'.

If the audit finds a caller that reads a top-level array, stop and comment on the task instead of changing that caller: it would be a design change.
implementationPlan.note: Audit of Invoke-MoeRpc callers (scripts/moe-agent.ps1 at this base, ~50 sites; read-only, no code change). Every daemon tool the wrapper calls answers a JSON object, so no real reply is a top-level array and no caller changes on real traffic. Only one-element or empty top-level arrays differ, and the daemon never sends them. Verdicts: (1) Discarded via | Out-Null or ignored, no change: 686 deregister_worker, 5324/8804/9594/9616/10345/11053/11060/11177/11317 chat_send, 6147 add_comment, 9385 chat_join. (2) Null-checked only, no change: 2838 chat_send, 3117 report_blocked, 5313 record_commit (returned to caller), 7563 add_comment, 8769 release_task, 9073 report_account_usage, 11007 report_account_usage, 9397 enter_governance. A real empty reply [] used to be $null and is now @(); none of these gets one. (3) Object-field readers, unchanged on objects: 2079 reattach_attempt and 2110 Send-MoeEvidence (record_candidate, record_check_run, record_delivery_receipt, finalize_attempt) go through Get-MoeProp, which sees no field on an array, so they take their failure branch ('invalid payload acknowledgement' for the evidence path). 4216 get_commit_scope tests PSObject.Properties['taskId'] and ['asserted'], so it falls to the disk fallback. 7258-7312 Invoke-MoeLandLeaseRpc (acquire/wait/release_resource) reads $r.granted, which is not a bool on an array, so kind='bad'. 7988 and 11107/11287 get_context, 9653 get_context, 8044 and 9374 chat_channels, 9387/9662 chat_read, 9389 get_pending_questions, 9420/9506 claim_next_task, 9445 chat_wait, 11149 list_tasks all read named fields (.task, .channels, .tasks) and see none on an array. 8877 lease_account is serialized with ConvertTo-Json and handed to the account helper, which rejects a non-lease reply. (4) 3181 get_execution_readiness (n1's gate) returns to today's path on -isnot PSCustomObject, which is the purpose of this fix. (5) Pass-throughs 1926 Invoke-MoeRpcUnserved and 7258 Invoke-MoeLandLeaseRpc return Invoke-MoeRpc output unchanged. No caller pipes, enumerates or wraps Invoke-MoeRpc output in @(); the only list read is $sibResp.tasks, a field of an object reply. No caller reads a top-level array.

implementationPlan.description:
Verification gate. Run it ONCE, fresh, after the last tracked edit. Its output is moe.complete_task's evidence: the command, exitCode and outputTail. It takes about 20-30 minutes, so start it with Bash run_in_background and wait for the completion notice instead of polling.

Run the executionContract checkRef exactly (byte-identical copy: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-044c/checkref.txt), from anywhere inside your task worktree:

( R=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) && F="$(wslpath -w "$R")\scripts\tests" && cd /mnt/d/moe-scratch && L=$(mktemp /mnt/d/moe-scratch/044c-gate.XXXX) && env $(env | grep -oE '^(MOE_|CLAUDE|FAKE_)[A-Za-z0-9_]*' | sed 's/^/-u /') MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 WSLENV=MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC bash -c 'powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$1\postflight-vm-route.ps1" && pwsh.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$1\postflight-vm-route.ps1" && powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "$1\postflight.ps1" && bash "$2/scripts/tests/parity-check.sh"' _ "$F" "$R" > "$L" 2>&1; r=$?; echo "log=$L exit=$r"; tr -d '\0\r' < "$L" | grep -axE 'PASS (postflight-vm-route\.ps1|postflight\.ps1|parity-check\.sh)' | sort | uniq -c; exit $r )

What it does: it runs YOUR worktree's harnesses by their D:\ path (wslpath -w), from a D: cwd. A /tmp cwd breaks postflight.ps1 (mem:gotcha-qa-ps1-postflight-from-wsl). Every MOE_*, CLAUDE* and FAKE_* variable is removed, and MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 is passed through WSLENV. The legs, in order:
1. postflight-vm-route.ps1 alone under Windows PowerShell 5.1;
2. postflight-vm-route.ps1 alone under pwsh 7;
3. postflight.ps1 under 5.1, which runs postflight-vm-route.ps1 again through n1's hook;
4. bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh, which also fails if moe-agent.ps1 lost its UTF-8 BOM (parity-check.sh:311).
The subshell exits with the chain's own code, not the trailing grep's.

Expected: `log=... exit=0`, then these counts:
- `3 PASS postflight-vm-route.ps1` (5.1 alone, 7 alone, nested);
- `1 PASS parity-check.sh`;
- `1 PASS postflight.ps1`.
A leg that never ran is missing from the counts, so check them. In the architect's dry run on n1's current bytes, postflight-vm-route.ps1 passed on 5.1 and on 7 (/mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-044c/summary.txt). The postflight.ps1 leg had not finished when this plan was submitted.

Global rails:
- Rail 1: never run npm or the daemon/proxy test suites in the shared checkout. This gate runs none.
- Rail 2: if a run hangs, kill only a PID your own session started, never by name. The harnesses already kill only their own wrapper PIDs with taskkill /T.

Error handling for a red run: read the log first.
- T-malformed-array fails: the fix is not in, or its text differs from the plan's.
- A refusal row fails: the change over-wraps objects (step 5's M4).
- postflight.ps1 fails anywhere else: rerun the parent revision's scripts (a scratch `git archive` of the base) before blaming the change, because the WSL launch environment can fail it on its own (mem:gotcha-qa-ps1-postflight-from-wsl).
Never weaken the command.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Invoke-MoeRpc (scripts/moe-agent.ps1) returns a tool reply in its wire shape on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7. A top-level JSON array, one-element and empty ones included, comes back as one array. Objects, scalars, null and non-JSON text come back exactly as before. So CQ-M07n1's readiness gate takes today's host path for the malformed reply [{"profile":"verified-local","ready":true,"missingCapabilities":[]}], the route the sh twin takes, instead of refusing as if a ready verified-local project had answered. No caller changes: every tool the wrapper calls answers a JSON object.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/tests/postflight-vm-route.ps1 gains the today-path row 'malformed-array' with the ruling's exact singleton reply. It passes under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7, with the host launch identical to the legacy baseline, and it fails on both engines without the fix.

Every existing postflight-vm-route.ps1 row passes unchanged on both engines, postflight.ps1 passes under 5.1, and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes; parity-check also proves moe-agent.ps1 keeps its UTF-8 BOM.

Objects, scalars, null, non-JSON text and arrays of two or more items come back from Invoke-MoeRpc exactly as before. Only one-element and empty top-level arrays change: they used to come back as their item or as $null, and now come back as one array.
The complete_task summary carries an audit of every Invoke-MoeRpc caller (call site, tool, how the reply is consumed, verdict) showing that no caller's behaviour changes on real replies.

A malformed readiness reply of any shape takes the same route on ps1 as on sh: today's path, per n1's DoD 1 and the governor's 16:31Z ruling on task-65b3e023. A well-formed object reply is unchanged: every refusal row still refuses.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) An opt-in switch on Invoke-MoeRpc (e.g. -NoEnumerate) used only by n1's gate: rejected. It leaves every other object consumer unrolling, it needs a call-site edit in n1's gate, and the audit found no list caller that the default-path fix could change. (2) Parsing through a wrapper object ('{"v":' + $text + '}').v: rejected. It is engine-neutral, but it changes how some invalid text parses. (3) Normalizing with @(...): rejected, because on pwsh 7 '[]' becomes @($null), a one-element array. (4) Also fixing Get-MoeProp's unrolling: rejected as out of scope (a separate helper, which n1 already avoids). (5) A separate AST-loaded drill file for Invoke-MoeRpc with CI wiring: rejected. The governor named the postflight-vm-route.ps1 rows, the refusal rows already catch over-wrapping (M4), and probe.ps1 covers the other shapes on both engines. (6) A matching sh row: not needed. The sh gate already treats a list as malformed (it calls .get on a list), and CQ-M07m3 may still edit postflight-vm-route.sh. (7) No dependsOn, as the governor first placed it: rejected. The row lives in n1's new file and tests n1's gate, and a worktree cut before n1 lands would never get them. It is a §8 PRODUCES edge; the governor was told in #governors and in a task comment.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: A PowerShell function return enumerates a collection, and pwsh 7's ConvertFrom-Json also enumerates unless -NoEnumerate, so before this fix a one-element array reached every caller as its item on both engines. On pwsh 7, '[[1]]' even came back as 1. `return ,$x` and `return Cmd` (a command's output object passes through as is) are the shape-preserving forms; the probe confirmed both on 5.1.26100 and 7.6.9. n1's harness (postflight-vm-route.ps1) drives the real wrapper per row with the shared fake proxy; FAKE_READINESS sets the readiness text, and the T rows compare the fake CLI's masked launch record with a legacy baseline. postflight.ps1 runs it nested through n1's 2-line hook.

If n1's landed gate differs (no type check before field reads), stop and comment. The gate takes 20-30 minutes on Windows engines, so run it in the background. Mutants run only on a /mnt/d/moe-scratch copy. On malformed replies only, a `$r.count`-style read of a one-element array now returns the array's length; that is acceptable because the daemon never sends arrays.
